findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None, raising AttributeError on every request
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally for every GET on this endpoint, before checking `use_optimized`. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional and is `None` when the requester is not a member of the organization (e.g. a superuser/staff user, or an org-auth-token/API-key request that passes the `OrganizationAuditPermission` check without membership). Because Python's `or` short-circuits only when the left side is truthy, a non-superuser non-member will dereference `None.has_global_access` and the endpoint will return a 500 instead of the audit log page. Guard with `use_optimized and organization_context.member is not None` (and only compute the flag inside the optimized branch).

findings.title: "authorized administrators" gate actually grants the feature to ordinary members
findings.body: The comment says the optimized path is for "authorized administrators", but the condition uses `organization_context.member.has_global_access`, which is true for any member of an organization with open membership (and for members whose role grants global access) — not just admins. Any such user can set `?optimized_pagination=true` and reach `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, which deliberately bypasses the offset lower-bound (see `paginator.py`). The access-control intent and the implemented check do not match; use an explicit admin/owner scope check if the feature is meant to be privileged, and fix the misleading comment.

findings.title: Negative queryset slice is not supported by Django and will raise, not "handled automatically"
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and the client supplies a cursor with a negative offset, `start_offset = cursor.offset` is negative and `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is executed. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indices (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), so this path can never work: it turns a user-controlled cursor value into an unhandled 500 instead of a `BadPaginationError`/400. The inline comment claiming "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually wrong. Either validate `offset >= 0` and raise `BadPaginationError`, or remove the feature.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes for datetime sort keys
findings.body: `get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to `getattr(item, self.key)`. The only caller added in this PR (`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`) uses `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime` and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. Every request with `?optimized_pagination=true` from an eligible user will 500 as soon as a cursor is built. Either subclass `DateTimePaginator`'s key conversion or do not use this paginator for datetime columns.

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns a raw number for a datetime column, producing an invalid WHERE clause
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged (integer/float), but `BasePaginator.build_queryset` injects it into `WHERE "auditlogentry"."datetime" >= %s`. For the audit-log endpoint the sort key is a timestamp column, so comparing it against a bare millisecond integer either raises a database error or silently filters wrong rows. `DateTimePaginator` converts the cursor value back to a `datetime` for exactly this reason; this subclass must do the same.

findings.title: Silent clamping of negative offsets changes pagination semantics and is inconsistent for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` in `BasePaginator.get_result` silently rewrites a client-supplied negative forward offset to 0, so the response no longer corresponds to the requested cursor; the next/prev cursors produced by `build_cursor` are still derived from the original (negative) `cursor.offset`, so clients can get duplicated or skipped rows instead of a clear error. Meanwhile the `is_prev` branch still passes a negative offset straight into the queryset slice, which Django rejects with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (500). Invalid offsets should be rejected uniformly with `BadPaginationError` rather than half-clamped.

findings.title: Comment claims a behavior change that the code does not make
findings.body: The added comment in `Cursor.__init__` ("Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios") describes a change, but the only code here is the pre-existing `self.offset = int(offset)`; nothing about negative offsets was enabled or validated. The comment misleads future readers into believing negative offsets are an intentionally supported/validated feature of `Cursor`, when in fact consumers such as `OffsetPaginator` still raise `BadPaginationError` for them. Remove or correct it.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new query parameter
findings.body: The PR adds a new public paginator class with its own `get_result` implementation and a new request-controlled branch in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` (`?optimized_pagination=true`), but no tests are added for either. The paginator's datetime key handling and negative-offset path are both broken (see other findings), which a single test exercising the endpoint with the new parameter would have caught. Add tests covering: the optimized branch for an eligible user, a non-member/superuser requester (where `organization_context.member` is None), and a negative-offset cursor.

findings.title: get_result duplicated from BasePaginator, dropping explanatory invariants
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result` (~60 lines) with the inline documentation about the extra before-row fetch removed. Any future fix to the base implementation (e.g. the cursor-value comparison edge case documented in the base method) will silently not apply here. Prefer overriding only the slice computation via a small hook instead of copying the whole method.
